issues.failure_explanation: By Parseval as stated later, the Fourier-domain misfit equals m^2 times the exit-wave misfit, so eqn:exit_misfit is 1/m^2 of eqn:data_misfit, not equal to it. The gradient and rate bounds are for this scaled exit objective.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing m^2 factor in eqn:exit_misfit or explicitly state that the paper uses the scaled exit-wave objective.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalence with the original data misfit is false; constants in gradients and convergence bounds refer to the scaled objective.
issues.title: Missing Parseval factor in objective equivalence
issues.why_classification: A local constant-factor correction; the minimizer and optimization conclusions are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\theta(0)$ is undefined, we set $\mathcal{R}_k(\bm{z}_k)_r = \mathcal{F}^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\bm{d}_k}\right)_r$ when $\mathcal{F}(\bm{Q}\odot \bm{z}_k)_r = 0$.

Note that this computation does not work when $\mathcal{F}(\bm{Q}\odot \bm{z}_k))_r=0$ at some index $r$.  This issue can be prevented by finding the gradient using the third statement of Proposition~\ref{prop:mm_cond}.

issues.failure_explanation: At an entry with F(Qz)_r=0 and d_r>0, the term (|F(Qz)_r|-sqrt(d_r))^2 has a modulus kink and is not differentiable in z. Defining R at the zero does not make Phi differentiable. The proof of gradient agreement assumes differentiability, so the claim is ill-defined/unsupported at such points; the appendix note referring back to this proposition is circular.

failure_location.quote: \item The complex gradients of $\Phi(\bm{z})$ and $\widetilde{\Phi}\left(\bm{z} ; \bm{z}^{(j)}\right)$ agree at $\bm{z}^{(j)}$:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either assume F(Qz)_r is never zero when d_r>0 at relevant iterates, or define a valid subgradient and adapt the gradient-based results to the nonsmooth case.
issues.overall_effect: Gradient-based optimality and stopping criteria are unreliable at points where a Fourier coefficient of the exit wave vanishes.
issues.title: Gradient agreement fails at zero Fourier entries
issues.why_classification: Handling zeros requires either a new subgradient framework or an added nondegeneracy assumption; the current proof is circular at those points.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only derives that equality of objective values forces the gradient to vanish. The reverse implication is false. For example, in scalar ptychography with N=1, Q=1, d=1 and z^0=2, the surrogate minimizer is z^1=1; then Phi(z^1)=0<Phi(z^0)=1/2 but grad Phi(z^1)=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the 'iff' by the valid implication 'if Phi(z^{j+1})=Phi(z^j) then grad Phi(z^{j+1})=0' or add an additional hypothesis for the converse.
issues.overall_effect: The optimality equivalence stated in the theorem is false; only the forward implication is supported.
issues.title: False equivalence between objective equality and zero gradient
issues.why_classification: The reverse implication is false, but the main monotonic descent and the forward implication survive; a limited weakening repairs it.

issues.failure_explanation: In the expansion of the surrogate difference, the linear term has coefficient 1/2. The next line drops this 1/2, doubling the linear term. With the correct factor, the chosen step gives only <=0, not -1/L||g||^2. The resulting bound is too strong; e.g., for m=1, Q=1, d=1, z^0=2 and n=0, the left side is 1 while the claimed right side is 0.25.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the dropped 1/2 in the proof, weaken the rate constant accordingly (e.g., 2C/(n+1) Phi(z^0)), and handle n=0.
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence-rate constant is not established and is false for n=0; a weaker constant is needed.
issues.title: Convergence-rate proof drops a factor of 1/2
issues.why_classification: A local algebra correction changes only a constant in the rate; the sublinear O(1/n) guarantee survives.

issues.failure_explanation: If Q_H=0 (possible even if fine Q entries are nonzero due to phase cancellation), then W_u^H=0, so u_H=0. The MGPS update divides by u+|Q|^2=0, giving 0/0. No convention for this degenerate case is specified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify a convention for the update when Q=0 and u+|Q|^2=0, e.g., set the update to zero.
issues.overall_effect: The recursive multigrid solver is not well defined for coarse probes with zero entries; the coarse-update formula in thm:coarse_grid_update has the same division.
issues.title: MGPS update is ill-defined when coarse probe and regularization vanish
issues.why_classification: A local degenerate-case convention restores well-definedness without changing the method's scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Iterates $\bm{z}^{(j)}$ delivered by the surrogate minimization (see~\eqref{eqn:surrogate_minimization}) converge sublinearly with respect to~\eqref{eqn:exit_misfit}:
Since the problem is inherently large-scale, the algorithm is run in a stochastic manner---scanning regions are shuffled per iteration and updated sequentially.

issues.failure_explanation: The monotonic descent and sublinear rate theorems are stated for exact full-batch surrogate minimization in eqn:surrogate_minimization. MGrPIE is stochastic, sequential, and uses proximal regularized updates; the paper only proves a coarse-grid descent direction for the fine surrogate, not global monotonic descent or sublinear convergence of MGrPIE. The conclusion therefore claims a guarantee for the proposed algorithm that is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Scope the convergence claim to the full-batch surrogate minimization, or provide a convergence proof for the stochastic proximal MGrPIE algorithm.
issues.overall_effect: The main algorithm's advertised convergence guarantee is unsupported; only the full-batch surrogate method has the stated convergence results.
issues.title: Convergence guarantees claimed for stochastic multigrid algorithm are not established
issues.why_classification: The overclaim concerns the main algorithm's theoretical guarantee; a clear scope restriction or new convergence proof is needed, but the surrogate analysis remains.

issues.failure_explanation: The computation shows the inner product equals -4(I_h^H g)^* diag(A) I_h^H g. Equality with 0 gives I_h^H g=0, not g=0. For example, a fine vector g with entries +1,-1,+1,-1 in one bin has zero average but is nonzero. Thus the equality implication is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality statement by 'equality implies I_h^H grad tilde Phi_k = 0' or remove the extra equality claim.
issues.overall_effect: The extra equality characterization in the descent proposition is false; the descent inequality itself remains valid.
issues.title: Equality in multigrid descent condition does not imply zero gradient
issues.why_classification: An extra equality claim not used for the descent conclusion; removing or weakening it is local.
